sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for upload checks
sections.what: Brings in the checks and documentation helpers used by the request descriptions below.

sections.name: DocumentTypeEnum
sections.title: Allowed document types
sections.what: Lists the document categories a user can choose, such as lab report, prescription, imaging and insurance.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list keeps document types consistent across the app.
sections.watch_out: This list must match the document type list in the database, or uploads with a new type will be refused or stored wrongly.

sections.name: GetUploadUrlDto
sections.title: Upload link request rules
sections.what: Describes the request for an upload link: a file name, a content type, a file size between 1 byte and 50 MB, and a document type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the size limit protects storage and upload time. The code comment records the 50 MB value.
sections.watch_out: The content type is not checked against allowed types, so any limit on file kinds must be enforced elsewhere, if at all.

sections.name: ConfirmUploadDto
sections.title: Confirm upload request rules
sections.what: Describes the request sent after an upload finishes: the file key from storage, the document type, and optional title, provider name and doctor name.
sections.why: Likely reason: the optional details let the user add context to a record without making them required.
sections.watch_out: The file key is only checked to be text, so this file does not prove that the key belongs to the signed-in user.

summary: Describes and checks the data the app sends when starting a document upload and when confirming one.
purpose: Stops bad upload requests early, such as oversized files, unknown document types, or empty file names.
why: Likely reason: checking on arrival keeps broken or oversized uploads away from storage. The 50 MB limit is stated in a code comment.
how: 1) The upload-link request must include a file name, a content type, a size between 1 byte and 50 MB, and a document type from the list. 2) The confirm request must include a file key and a document type, and may include a title, provider name and doctor name. 3) Checks run when a request arrives, and the API documentation is produced from the same descriptions.
inputs: Upload details from the app: file name, content type, file size, document type, file key, and the optional title, provider name and doctor name.
outputs: Checked request objects for the document service, or a validation error returned to the caller.
risks: The content type is only checked to be present, so any file type is accepted at this step. The document type list here is separate from the database list, so the two can drift apart. The optional name fields have no maximum length.
debug: If an upload is rejected, read the validation message. A size error means the file is over 50 MB or is empty. If a new document type is refused, add it to the list here and check the database list too.
